deepdive.sec: Premium Residential Real Estate & Integrated Construction

bull_bear.body: Net-cash balance sheet (net-debt ratio −0.14) with low 7.62% borrowing cost. Prioritizes: strong/liquid balance sheet, improved collections, disciplined land acquisition. INR1,000cr NCDs approved for tranche-wise acquisition funding. No dividend/buyback commentary. Balances land aggression against maintaining ~0 net debt for the year.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Margin execution:** H2 17-20% target is a repeat of last quarter's H2-revival guidance — must actually land via completions.
- **Collections lag:** presales strong but Q1 collections modest (quarter-end skew + labour-driven milestone-billing shortfall).
- **Labour:** Karnataka +60% min-wage cost impact "yet to be assessed"; April-May shortage affected billing.
- **Mix dilution:** rising joint-development share lowers marginal cash-flow margins vs own-land projects.
- **Launch/approval slippage:** Mumbai timing uncertain; overall growth depends on launches landing on schedule.
- **Supply/cycle:** demand "stable/reasonably good"; management watching how competing supply develops.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and execution-focused; attributes the strong quarter to launch preparation, not just market timing. Transparent about the collections shortfall, the labour issue, the margin trough, and the marginal-cash-flow reduction (JD mix + Hoskote roll-off). Reiterates prudence — net-cash discipline, tranche-wise NCDs, absorbing wage inflation within budgets.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- Headline presales (+76%) far outrun revenue (+48%) and collections — the value is stored in the INR20,553cr unrecognized backlog; the earnings/margin inflection is a completion-driven H2/FY27 event, not a Q1 one.
- The forthcoming-project margin cut (INR86bn→INR68.3bn) is structural (more JD, less own-land like Hoskote) — a quieter negative under the record-presales headline.
- Net cash of only INR659cr despite record sales reflects deliberate front-loaded land investment (net outflow INR149cr in the quarter) — growth capex, not weakness.
- Gurgaon commercial asset possibly shifting from sale to rental annuity — a small model-mix signal worth tracking.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Net cash balance sheet: Net Debt of (INR 6.59) Bn at Q1 FY27 - "Net cash positive" - with Gross Debt of INR 11.10 Bn against cash equivalents of INR 17.69 Bn; net debt moved from INR 23.37 Bn (FY22), 16.40 (FY23), 12.62 (FY24) to (6.30) FY25, (8.08) FY26 and (6.59) Q1 FY27.
- D/E Ratio of (0.14) at Q1 FY27, "from 0.97 in FY22" (0.66 FY23, 0.50 FY24, (0.14) / (0.17) / (0.14) in the later periods shown).
- Deleveraging was funded by equity: in 2024 SOBHA "Successfully raises Rs 20 billion via a rights issue" (FY25 cash equivalents shown as including rights issue receipts).
- Credit rating of AA-: "Ind-RA upgraded Outlook" to Positive, and "ICRA AA- Stable".
- Cash returned is modest relative to reinvestment: dividend outflow of INR 322 Mn in FY-26 and nil in Q1-27 and Q4-26, against Net Land Payments of INR 11,603 Mn in FY-26.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Residential (core):** SOBHA One World (3,484 homes / 47.4 acres; released 3.4 msf, sold ~40% at launch; 45% of quarter's sales); SOBHA Crescent Gurgaon (~60% sold in Q1); Sacred Grove (plotted, Bangalore); Rivana (Noida) steady post-launch.
- **Contractual, manufacturing & retail (backward integration):** ~INR170-171cr revenue; good order-book visibility; differentiator vs peers; FY27 run-rate ~flat vs FY26.
- **Commercial rental:** ~INR23cr total income; evaluating retaining a ~0.6 msf Gurgaon commercial project for rental (removed from sale pipeline pending decision).
- **New BD this quarter:** Mumbai (1.3 acres, INR180cr outright) + Greater Noida (JV, authority+landowner dues paid); combined GDV ~INR2,700-3,000cr.

business.body:
- Founded on the philosophy of "Passion at Work", incorporated 7 August 1995 by Mr. PNC Menon; "Over 30 years of delivering international-quality real estate", Bengaluru-headquartered with a strong focus on residential real estate.
- Backward integration is the stated moat: a "Fully integrated business model with end-to-end development capabilities" spanning Real Estate (Residential, Commercial, Institutional), Retail (Commercial), Contracting (Glazing & Metal Works, Interiors) and Manufacturing (Concrete Products, Mattresses, metercube).
- Quality credentials: first Indian real estate company to obtain ISO 9001 certification (1998); certified for ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015 and ISO 45001:2018; "Recipient of 272 awards for excellence in business, quality, leadership, sustainability and CSR"; ranked India's 'Top National Realty Brand' for the fifth consecutive year by Track2Realty's BrandXReport 2018-19.
- Geographic spread built over three decades: 28 cities and 14 states across India, with entries into Coimbatore (1997), Pune (2007), Thrissur (2008), Delhi-NCR and Mysuru (2011), Chennai (2012), Kozhikode (2014), Kochi (2016), Gujarat (2019), Thiruvananthapuram (2022) and Hyderabad (2023).
- Framed as "Built on a foundation of execution excellence, financial resilience and principle of disciplined growth" / "Transforming Strength to Sustainable Performance".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Future value drivers] The deck guides to INR 205.53 Bn of "revenue to be recognized from sold units", "30%+ projected project level EBITDA margin" and INR 194.81 Bn "marginal Cashflow from current & forthcoming projects" (Completed, Ongoing & Forthcoming) - note this project-level margin is a projection and is labelled differently from the reported Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin of 9.7%.
- [Inventory visibility] Total inventory visibility of 35.71 Mn sft SBA with total sales value of INR 531.99 Bn - completed projects 0.26 Mn sft / INR 2.26 Bn, ongoing released 10.18 Mn sft / INR 166.47 Bn, ongoing unreleased 4.50 Mn sft / INR 67.69 Bn, forthcoming residential 20.77 Mn sft / INR 295.57 Bn.
- [Economic interest] "SOBHA share in inventory of completed and ongoing projects is 81.3%" and "SOBHA share in total forthcoming projects inventory is 74.9%"; SOBHA share of Q1 FY27 sale value was INR 29.92 Bn, "81.8% of total sale". All reported future cash inflows are stated to be net of JD partner payments.
- [JD model] Joint Development Partner payments are a standing cash outflow line - INR 3,143 Mn in Q1-27 and INR 11,903 Mn in FY-26 - so a material share of the pipeline is on revenue-sharing/JD land rather than owned land.
- [Rental annuity] "NOI from operating commercial portfolio in Q1 FY27 was INR 146 Mn".
- [Leadership] Ravi PNC Menon is Chairman (24+ years' experience), Jagadish Nangineni Managing Director (IIT Bombay / IIM Calcutta) and Nisanth M N Deputy Managing Director; the founder is Mr. PNC Menon.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Reported EBITDA ~9.7% is the trough; margin expansion thesis rests on completing high-margin FY23-vintage projects (revenue recognized on completion). Forthcoming-project marginal cash flow guidance cut to INR68.3bn (from ~INR86bn) due to (a) higher joint-development mix and (b) high-margin own-land Hoskote rolling off the forthcoming set. Cost pressure: Karnataka minimum-wage +60% (May) under evaluation — technician force largely above minimum wage, expected to be absorbed within project budgets. April-May labour shortage delayed some completion milestones.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** Record presales INR3,656cr (+76%); revenue INR1,330cr (+48%); PAT INR50.7cr (vs INR13.5cr); EBITDA ~9.7%; net cash INR659cr (net-debt −0.14); unrecognized sold-revenue INR20,553cr; land spend INR370cr (FY27 target ~INR1,500-1,600cr); INR1,000cr NCDs approved. New BD: Mumbai + Greater Noida (GDV ~INR2,700-3,000cr). Guided FY27 presales ≥+30%, margin 17-20% by exit-Q4, completions 6-6.5 msf, 8.2 msf launches remaining.
- _Q2 FY27 → check: presales tracking ≥30%? Margin moving off 9.7% toward H2 target? Collections catch-up on Q1 sales? Launch schedule (Crescent Ph-2, Greater Noida, Hyderabad/Kerala) on time? Land spend vs INR1,500-1,600cr; NCD draw; wage-cost absorption._
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)

outlook.body:
- **Presales growth:** at least +30% for FY27 (possibly slightly better if launches land on time).
- **Margin:** significantly better sequentially in H2; Q2 similar to Q1 (~depends on completions); by exit-Q4 targeting ~17-20% EBITDA (from ~9.7% now).
- **Launches:** 9 projects / ~8.2 msf in remaining FY27 (~INR12,000cr GDV) — 4 Bangalore (~3 msf), 2 NCR (~2 msf), 1 Hyderabad (~1.7 msf), 2 Kerala (~1.5 msf). Crescent Phase-2 late-Q3/Q4; Greater Noida to launch this FY.
- **Completions:** 6-6.5 msf in FY27 vs 5.4 msf FY26 (~20% higher).
- **Net debt:** to remain ~0 (net-cash) for the year.
- **Land capex:** ~INR1,500-1,600cr for FY27 (vs INR1,160cr FY26); INR370cr already spent in Q1.
- **Operating cash flow:** aiming toward ~INR2,000cr (marginal, averaged over next few years).
- **Other businesses (contractual/mfg/rental):** FY27 revenue ~similar to FY26.
- **Funding:** INR1,000cr NCDs approved — to be drawn in ≥2 tranches over next couple of quarters as acquisitions firm up.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body:
- Forthcoming launch pipeline: 20.77 msf across 17 projects; near-term confident set = 9 projects / 8.2 msf in FY27.
- Unsold inventory: 14.94 msf.
- Q1 launches (3 projects, Bangalore+Gurgaon): 6.89 msf combined, ~INR10,000cr potential sale value.
- Unrecognized sold-revenue backlog INR20,553cr underpins multi-year revenue visibility.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- Geographic expansion into high-growth micro-markets (NCR scaling to highest-ever; Hyderabad, Kerala, new Mumbai foothold).
- Optionality to convert the Gurgaon commercial asset (full TDR in hand) into a rental annuity rather than sale.
- Land-bank build-out (INR1,500-1,600cr FY27) — greater joint-development mix lowers capital intensity but also lowers marginal cash-flow margin.
